The provided text explores the tension between societal expectations and personal desires in *Pride and Prejudice*, highlighting how different reader backgrounds shape their interpretation of the narrative. From a feminist perspective, readers may view Elizabeth Bennet as an empowering figure who asserts her agency against restrictive gender norms, celebrating her resistance to marrying solely for security. Conversely, traditionalist readers might interpret the same events through the lens of social stability, valuing the characters' emphasis on reputation, class, and familial duty as necessary components of a functioning society. This duality illustrates that literature is not static; its meaning shifts depending on whether the reader prioritizes individual autonomy or collective social order.
